title: Effect of register-only head moves
statement: Let a configuration with input $x$ have state $st$, input-head position $ip$, register tapes $rt$ and head positions $rp$, decider tapes $dt$ and head positions $dp$, and output $out$. Given an input-head movement $mv_I$ and a movement sign $f(r)$ for each register $r$, an action that makes those moves, leaves all tape contents unchanged, emits no output, and enters state $st'$ sends the configuration to one with state $st'$, input-head position moved by the clamped move $mv_I$, register-head positions $rp(r)+f(r)$, and the decider tapes and all other listed data unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: $m,d,k_D$ are natural numbers; $\Lambda,SD$ are state types
$st$ is an optional program state and $st'$ is a program state
$rt,dt$ are tape-content functions and $rp,dp$ are head-position functions
$f$ assigns a movement sign to each register
